news.title: Argentina confirm CAS appeal after FIFA uphold Leandro Paredes' 10-match ban and $321,000 fine over World Cup final chaos
news.lede: Argentina will take their fight against FIFA's World Cup final sanctions to the Court of Arbitration for Sport after the governing body's appeals committee upheld Leandro Paredes' 10-match ban and a $321,000 fine on the national federation. Nahuel Molina did see his suspension reduced, but the federation insist they have the arguments to overturn the remaining punishments. Argentina confirm CAS appeal over World Cup final sanctions The Argentine Football Association (AFA) announced on Saturday that they will appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions handed out by FIFA following the ugly scenes at the end of the 2026 World Cup final.

news.title: Argentina FA set to go to Cas after Fifa rejects appeals over 2026 World cup incidents
news.lede: Leandro Paredes (centre), Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada all appeared to be involved in a fracas on the pitch after Spain won their World Cup final. The Argentina Football Association says it is planning to apply to the Court of Arbitration for Sport over Fifa rejecting its appeals against punishments handed out to the organisation and midfielder Leandro Paredes. Paredes was given a 10-match ban for his role in on-field clashes following Argentina's 1-0 defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. Team-mate Nahuel Molina was given a seven-game ban, with both players being fined $90,000 (£66,000), and while the AFA said Molina's suspension had been reduced to four games by Fifa, the sanctions on Paredes stood.

news.title: Argentina Football Association Appeals FIFA Sanctions Over World Cup Final Brawl
news.lede: Leandro Parades was sent off after the game after starting a brawl with some of Spain's players. Photo: Sky Sports Argentina’s football association announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents. Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit, with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players. He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19.

news.title: Gianni Infantino ‘Cancels Another Controversial World Cup Plan’ After Election Rival Emerges
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino is reported to have abandoned plans to further expand the World Cup from 48 to 64 teams as he prepares to fight for his future in the upcoming elections. Infantino had been expected to run unopposed for another term in charge of soccer’s governing body, only for a controversial proposal to sell shares in future tournaments to send his approval ratings plummeting and raise questions about his continuation. Now, The Times state Infantino has also privately confirmed he will not pursue plans to take the World Cup up to 64 teams, with the move believed to be part of a plan to try and win over his doubters. That comes shortly after it was confirmed that Kozo Tashima, honorary chairman of the Japan Football Association (JFA), plans to run against Infantino in the next elections in March 2027.

news.title: World Cup final brawl: FIFA reduces Molina’s ban, upholds Paredes’ suspension
news.lede: The FIFA Appeals Chamber has reduced Argentina defender Nahuel Molina’s suspension from seven matches to four, while upholding the 10-match ban imposed on midfielder Leandro Paredes following disciplinary incidents during Spain’s World Cup celebrations. The Argentine Football Association (AFA) announced the decisions on Friday night, confirming that Molina’s punishment had been reduced following an appeal. The right-back, who was initially handed a seven-match suspension for punching Rodri during Spain’s celebrations after their 1-0 World Cup final victory, will now serve a four-match ban and pay a fine of $60,000. However, Paredes failed to secure a reduction in his punishment.

news.title: Because of the 2030 World Cup: Lekjaa takes an important decision regarding his position within CAF
news.lede: Fawzi Lekjaa looks set to reshuffle his cards within the Confederation of African Football. The move could bring an end to one of his most prominent roles in the corridors of African football, with the Moroccan moving towards resigning from the presidency of CAF's finance committee while keeping his position as first vice-president of the continental body. Moroccan website Hespport report that Lekjaa has decided to step down from the finance committee presidency because of the sheer weight of commitments the role brings. The frequent travel is part of it, as is the considerable time needed to follow up the various files tied to running CAF's financial affairs.
